correctness.rationale: The angular expansion of f0+bar(z)f1 exhausts the full space: one scalar sector at -1 and two dimensions per nonnegative mode. With x=n+1, the truncated beta law normalized by q^x is the law of qS for S~Beta(x,1). For the standardized degree-one polynomial, this gives compressed first moment −sqrt(x(x+2))(1−q) and compressed second moment q²+x(x+2)(1−q)² after division by q^x. In multiplying the two matrices the cross-terms linear in their diagonal differences cancel, leaving the signed (r−q) factor claimed. Each positive branch has two singular values, and coincident branch values add multiplicities; no simplicity across different modes is required. All these blocks are invertible for distinct cutoffs, so the scalar sector gives the complete kernel. Exponential decay proves fixed-cutoff Schatten membership. The exact formula on the u=epsilon(n+1) grid converges uniformly on interior compacta, with envelope ab|a−b|(u+epsilon)^3 exp(−(a+b)u); this controls both tails of power sums and maxima. The limiting maximum is at u=3/(a+b), and the rate optimization reduces to maximizing w(1−w²), with w=|a−b|/(a+b). Strong convergence of the compressions follows by dominated convergence on each vector and uniform contractivity. Independent 40-digit quadrature of the moments gave signed block entries .122213505, .0270662057 and .008350872055 at (n,q,r)=(0,.3,.7),(5,.42,.91),(19,.7,.93), matching the formula to within 3e−42 at working precision. For rates (1,3) and epsilon=.001, independently summed finite-mode ratios to the analytic limits were .999990920, .999999250 and .999999033 for powers 1/4, 1 and 2; the norm ratio was .999999694. These are corroboration only; the supplied checker was inspected, not executed.

originality.rationale: The general block representation is established prior work, and the finite-cutoff formula is an explicit low-degree evaluation of it, not a new diagonalization theorem. The surviving main contribution is the moving two-cutoff spectral profile with sharp norm and all-Schatten constants; no covering result was identified in inspected material. In particular, compactness for each pair does not decide whether the pairwise commutator retains order-one norm when both cutoffs move.
residual_risks: The 2025 quasihomogeneous-symbol article could cover some finite-cutoff algebra or commutation implications; access did not permit a full-text comparison.

A broader step-symbol spectral theorem or an unindexed exact cutoff calculation may exist. This assessment assigns no priority to the known Jacobi matrix framework or simple fixed-cutoff consequences.

value.rationale: The full bianalytic space is the first radial Bergman setting with genuine matrix-valued fibers. Two increasing concentration regions provide a natural test of whether compressions becoming identities retain noncommutativity. The result locates the escaping order-one modes, quantifies their combined mass at all powers, and determines the sharp rate ratio rather than merely exhibiting two operators that fail to commute.
